inputs.text: Taylor is drawing a line against even discussing higher taxes on gas companies or reducing property investor concessions—exactly the sort of “open-minded” debate that might threaten powerful interests. His refusal to echo Hastie on Trump or say whether he supports the US and Israel’s war with Iran looks less like uncertainty than a careful effort to avoid upsetting people who matter. With MPs already talking about leadership, this is factional positioning dressed up as a policy clash: the party’s insiders are managing what can be questioned, and who gets to lead.
